articles.title: UK, Ukraine sign AI defence partnership linked to battlefield technology
articles.body:
Britain, Ukraine sign AI defence partnership linked to battlefield technology
LONDON – Britain said on Aug 24 it had signed a partnership with Ukraine to jointly develop artificial intelligence tools for defence and security, giving British researchers access to a Ukrainian battlefield data platform used to train military AI systems.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky signed the agreement in Kyiv, making Britain the first international partner to access Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs, a government statement said.
Avengers Labs was built around an annotated dataset of five million battlefield images, Ukraine’s Defence Ministry said earlier in August, largely drawn from the military’s DELTA combat system – a domestically developed battlefield management and situational-awareness system.
The platform uses data collected from cameras and sensors across Ukraine’s battlefield, including information on tanks, artillery systems, drones and other military targets.
The Ukrainian ministry said AI models trained on the data were already being used in an automated target-detection system that analyses more than 100,000 drone video feeds each month and can identify about 70 per cent of enemy targets in real time.
Under the deal, Britain and Ukraine will collaborate on pilot projects including technology that uses fibre-optic cables as AI-enabled sensors to help protect military facilities, and research into low-power AI chips for drones and autonomous systems.
The British government said the partnership would initially focus on defence and national security projects bringing together researchers, engineers, technology companies and military experts from both countries.
Burnham on Aug 24 visited Ukraine for his first trip abroad since becoming prime minister, where he had talks with Zelensky and co-chaired a meeting of the “Coalition of the Willing”.
His office had earlier announced Britain would allow missile maker MBDA to release classified information on British-made components used in the SCALP long-range cruise missile to help establish assembly lines in Ukraine. REUTERS

articles.title: Russia will 'try to escalate' against Europe to deter Ukraine support: Macron
articles.body:
Şeyma Erkul Dayanç
24 August 2026•Update: 24 August 2026
Russia will seek to escalate against European countries to deter support for Ukraine, French President Emmanuel Macron warned Monday as European leaders gathered in Kyiv.
“Russia will try to escalate against European countries in order to deter them from assisting Ukraine,” Macron said at a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing.
“It’s clear that NATO countries will be targeted and the provocations will multiply,” he added, calling for a “robust posture” from European allies.
Macron said France and its partners should accelerate deliveries of air defense interceptors and anti-ballistic missile capabilities to Ukraine.
He warned that shortages of such systems have “direct consequences on people's lives.”
Macron said France would accelerate deliveries of available systems and work with partners to increase production capacity in Ukraine.
He also called for continued support for Ukraine's energy sector ahead of winter and faster disbursement of financial assistance to support the country's budget.
On pressure against Russia, Macron said allies must step up efforts against the so-called shadow fleet used to circumvent sanctions.
 
“We must double down on our efforts regarding sanctions and respective measures and strengthen our coordination,” he said.
Macron proposed a ministerial meeting in the coming weeks focused on measures against the shadow fleet.
He also urged allies to prepare new sanctions targeting Russian oil and gas imports.
Macron said Russia has increasingly turned to imports from third countries following measures against its shadow fleet.
On security guarantees, Macron said the Coalition of the Willing would conduct a full-scale exercise in October and November to demonstrate its operational preparedness and ability to act once hostilities cease.

articles.title: US Launching 'Economic Onslaught' On Iran, Demands Countries Cut 'Lifelines' That Sustain Tehran
articles.body:
WASHINGTON -- US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a new effort to ramp up the pressure on Tehran, saying the United States is "launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe."
"Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent told a news conference on August 24, days after he and President Donald Trump warned of an "economic D-Day."
The announcement came nearly six months after the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has roiled global markets by choking off oil supplies from the Persian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz.
The US is "ending" the threat from Iran rather than "managing" it, Bessent asserted, warning third countries that the United States will "be uncompromising in targeting any source of the [Iranian] regime's illicit revenue."
Bessent said that Trump was making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests, and that ever country would be given a defined timeline to "shut down...Iran-related activity we have identified."
He declined to specify timelines but said "we do not have infinite pattence here."
The US Treasury Department has "mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror," Bessent said, and the US "will be uncompromising in targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue.
The Treasury Department said it had identified five sectors that Iran is using to prop up its economy -- digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping -- and is imposing new sanctions on nearly 60 entities, individuals, and vessels.
Any country supporting Iran must be prepared to face US sanctions, he said, while "the Iranian regime faces a clear choice: severe global isolation or a path to reintegration with the global economy."
"We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime," Bessent said.
Telegraphing the new effort last week without giving details, Bessent suggested that the existing US blockade on Iranan ports combined with what he said would be "the toughest sanctions in history" would make new military operations against Iran less likely to be needed.
But defense chief Pete Hegseth stressed that the use of military force was not being ruled out. "By no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran," he told reporters.
Large-scale attacks have abated, but on-again, off-again negotiations have not produced an agreement to end the war, free up the Strait of Hormuz, which handled 20 percent of global oil shipments before the war, or resolve the decades-old dispute over Iran's nuclear activities.
When asked whether the US would target China for continuing to buy Iranian oil, Bessent said, We are confident that everyone wants the Strait reopened, and for energy prices to come back down."
Separately, he said, "Keep in mind that the Chinese get 50 percent [of their] energy from inside the Gulf. So it would do them a big service to get with the program."
Earlier on August 24, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said, “Sanctions and pressure will not help resolve problems. They will only heighten tensions and escalate the situation, which serves no party's interests."
In comments quoted by the China Daily, Lin urged those involved to return to dialogue as soon as possible and seek a political settlement. Trump is sceduled to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington in late September.
In comments to broadcaster CNBC last week about the new measures, Bessent said, "We are going to collapse this regime." Trump, in a social media post on August 24, wrote: "IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING."
Iran's economy minister told state television that Tehran was anticipating new US measures and is "ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events."
"They have done everything they could to test the determination of the Iranian people and the country's officials, but they have failed every time. It seems they wished to suffer yet another defeat," Ali Madanizadeh said.
In a sign of persistent trouble for Iran's battered economy, however, the country's rial currency fell to a new low against the US dollar on the open market on August 24.
Mehdi Ghodsi, senior economist at the Vienna Institute for International Economic Studies, suggested that sanctions may not produce the produce the political response Washington expects.
“The government is much more stubborn than this," Ghodsi told RFE/RL. "The war has killed many of the regime's leaders and destroyed much of its infrastructure, but the government still sticks to its position.”
“The country is heading in a direction where nothing but destruction awaits it,” he said, but added: “For those running the country, it doesn't really matter where the country is heading."

articles.title: US threatens severe sanctions against countries with economic ties to Iran
articles.body:
The US has threatened to impose severe sanctions against any country or entity maintaining economic ties with Iran, hoping to achieve with economic measures what military means have so far failed to do.
It is unclear, however, how far the Trump administration is prepared to go in confronting China, Iran’s biggest trading partner, which has signalled its resistance to US economic pressure to cut off links with an ally.
Iran, meanwhile, vowed retaliation against any country that took part in the US-led isolation campaign.
Launching what he called Operation Economic Outcast, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, called it an unprecedented campaign and compared it with the D-day Normandy landings, a turning point in the second world war.
“Today, in that same spirit, we are launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe,” Bessent said on Monday. “Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone.”
Asked whether sanctions would be applied to China, which bought an estimated 80% of Iran’s shipped oil last year, he replied: “We want to make clear here today that no one is above the reach of US sanctions. That if they facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted.”
Bessent said the US had identified those that continued to deal with Iran and each violator would be given a deadline to cut ties or face US sanctions. He said the deadlines imposed would depend on individual circumstances.
“Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system,” he said. “The clock just started ticking.”
Bessent said Donald Trump was “making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests to cease their interactions with the regime”, but he did not specify whether the US president would talk to his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping.
China’s embassy in Washington told reporters: “Regarding the Iran issue, sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem. China calls on the relevant parties to take responsible actions and resolve the issue through political and diplomatic means.”
Tehran said it would retaliate against the sanctions using a range of measures. Maj Gen Ali Abdollahi, the armed forces’ chief of staff, said the retaliation could take the form of land, sea or air operations or cyber-attacks.
The announcement of secondary sanctions against Iran comes nearly six months after the the US and Israel launched an attack on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Early expectations that the regime in Tehran would collapse or agree to Washington’s demands to give up uranium enrichment and other key elements of its nuclear programme were dashed.
Hardliners appeared to strengthen their grip on government in Tehran and responded by declaring the closure of the strait of Hormuz, attacking ships that ignored its declaration. Trump imposed a counter-blockage on Iranian oil exports through the strait, leading to an impasse that has had profound effects on the global economy.
Sina Toossi, a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, said: “After nearly six months without a military or diplomatic victory, Washington appears to be trying to accomplish through intensified economic strangulation what military force has so far failed to achieve. But Tehran is answering that zero-sum approach with one of its own.”
The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, however, said further military action was not off the table. “By no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the strait of Hormuz or around Iran,” Hegseth told reporters on Monday.
In apparent anticipation of the US measures, the United Arab Emirates, a close US and Israeli ally, announced it was suspending trade ties with Iran. Turkey, another trading partner with Iran, which has been critical of the US-led campaign against the Islamic Republic, has yet to respond to the US threat of sanctions.
Andrew Miller, a senior fellow at the Center for American Progress, said: “The announcement of new economic sanctions on Iran and those countries trading with it signals what is plain to all: this war has brought the United States no closer to eliminating Iran’s nuclear programme or crippling the Iranian regime. But while sanctions can be effective, it is highly unlikely they will produce a quick settlement favourable to the United States.”

articles.title: Second Russian MiG-29 in two days: Ukraine’s drones worked over Millerovo airbase
articles.body:
Ukrainian drones worked over dozens of Russian military and industrial sites overnight on 24 August, reaching from occupied Ukraine and the Black Sea to southern Russia, the commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (SBS) reported. The night's targets included a fighter jet at a Russian airbase, air-defense radars, fuel and propellant facilities, and vessels of Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet. A fuller breakdown released later in the day named the site of each strike and the unit that carried it out. Footage released with the breakdown shows the strikes.
Ukraine has been running mid-range strikes across the belt from occupied Crimea to Rostov Oblast for months, taking out the radars, missile batteries, and the aircraft that fly air-defense patrols over it — a rolling effort to thin the cover that meets every deeper Ukrainian strike.
A fighter jet and a decoy at the same airbase
Robert Brovdi, callsign Madyar, said his crews hit 66 targets in the operational depth of the Russian rear. Among them was a MiG-29 at Dolotinka, on the grounds of the Millerovo airbase in Rostov Oblast. The 1st Separate Center of the SBS carried out that strike.
The same unit hit a mockup of a Ka-52 Alligator attack helicopter at the same location. Russia uses such decoys to draw drones away from real aircraft.
Ukraine’s drones hit two Russian fighters and a spy drone—and blinded radars from occupied Crimea to Rostov
It was the third Russian fighter jet Ukrainian drones reached in two days. Crews struck another MiG-29, a jet SBS identified as a Su-33 and Militarnyi assessed as a Su-30SM, and an Orion strike-reconnaissance drone at Vityazevo in Krasnodar Krai on 23 August. Ukrainian drones have caught a MiG-29 on a Russian airfield before, at Kursk in July.
Four radars, from Rostov Oblast to occupied Crimea
Crews hit four radar systems overnight. Two Kasta-2E2 sets went down at Geraskin and Karaichev in Rostov Oblast, and a Nebo-SV at Gukovo in the same oblast. All three fell to the 1st Separate Center.
The fourth, an ST-68, stood at Rozdolne in occupied Crimea. The 9th Kairos battalion of the 414th Madyar's Birds brigade struck it.
The radar work is part of a campaign against Russian sensors and launchers that has run for months without a pause.
Rocket propellant, fuel, and two ships
The 1st Separate Center struck the Kamensky Combine at Kamensk-Shakhtinsky in Rostov Oblast, a plant producing solid rocket fuel, according to SBS. The 9th Kairos battalion hit a fuel tank at Yeysk in Krasnodar Krai. In occupied Luhansk Oblast, the 20th K-2 brigade struck a fuel depot belonging to the 106th material support brigade of Russia's 41st Army at Dovzhansk.
Brovdi also said his crews hit and destroyed two shadow-fleet vessels, a tanker and a bulk carrier, in the Black Sea. No independent account of either loss has appeared.
A drone school, relays, and a base in occupied Kherson Oblast
In occupied Kherson Oblast, Ukrainian crews destroyed the quarters of a Russian National Guard rapid-response unit and hit two relay stations for Geran attack drones, according to the SBS breakdown.
They also struck a shelter for a Zala reconnaissance drone crew in occupied Crimea, a drone school in occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and a drone laboratory in occupied Donetsk Oblast.
Brovdi also reported 11 Russian rear deployment points burning across occupied Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk oblasts, along with strikes on energy nodes in occupied territory.

articles.title: The Vatican wants a seat at the Ukraine peace table. Here’s why
articles.body:
The Vatican wants a seat at the Ukraine peace table. Here’s why
The head of the Vatican’s diplomatic service, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, is visiting Moscow from August 24-28. This visit is part of the Holy See’s diplomatic efforts on humanitarian issues and the discussion of ways to resolve the Ukraine conflict. This is reflected in the fact that the Vatican, together with the authorities of several states, including Bulgaria, Hungary, and Italy recently contributed to keeping Patriarch Kirill off the latest EU sanctions list.
The visit is clearly necessary to revitalize communication between the Vatican and Moscow, as the formal diplomatic channels – though fully operational – have recently lost the historical depth and back-channel confidentiality previously maintained through the Russian Orthodox Church’s external relations. Below, we examine the true operational motives behind the Holy See’s urgent mission within the broader context of its geopolitical and financial survival in Central and Eastern Europe.
American Pope
Pope Leo XIV has been in power for a year, allowing us to draw certain conclusions about his leadership style. We see a tough, sovereign politician who skillfully uses conservative symbols to promote the Church’s internal stability, but on the world stage, he advocates a center-left, global agenda that criticizes both rigid state borders and the power of algorithms.
For example, the Vatican has returned to the use of traditional ornate vestments, which had been shelved under Francis XII. The public appearance was also received extremely favorably by conservative critics of the use of 'gender ideology' in schools and the promotion of non-traditional lifestyles. At the same time, the Pope is promoting ideas for decentralizing Vatican authority and proposing synodal reform, the essence of which is aimed at collegial governance of the Church, where decisions are made collectively by a large number of bishops and laypeople.
Most notable, however, have been his public disputes with various factions of his compatriots on the right; he has publicly criticized the immigration policies of US President Donald Trump’s administration and US Vice President J.D. Vance. In his first encyclical, Leo XIV harshly criticized artificial intelligence, calling for the “disarmament” of technology, a ban on its use for military purposes, and an end to the IT corporations’ proverbial race to the bottom, arguing that it could result in mass unemployment and that people could use it to escape into an “illusory world.”
Importantly, his statements provoked a counterattack from Silicon Valley leaders; Marc Andreessen and Peter Thiel were among those who reacted negatively.
Overall, this paints him as a representative of the systemic wing of the Catholic Church – a supranational sovereign structure that thinks in terms of centuries, not electoral cycles. His accession to the throne signaled the Roman Curia’s intention to establish a strict leader from the New World, free from parochial European caste disputes.
The Institute for the Works of Religion, aka the Vatican Bank: Personnel Changes and Conservatism
It’s logical that Pope Leo XIV began his sovereign expansion on the throne not with abstract peace declarations, but with an immediate, surgical reformatting of the Holy See’s entire financial vertical. His very first significant document was the Apostolic Letter ‘Coniuncta Cura’ (Joint Care), which dealt a crushing blow to the former monopoly over the Institute for the Affairs of Religion (IOR). The Pontiff officially rescinded Francis’s harsh decree, which had previously forcibly locked 100% of the liquidity of all Vatican departments and orders within the Vatican Bank.
Why did Leo XIV make this sensitive issue his very first priority? The answer is cynical: the previous centralization of accounts in the IOR had completely paralyzed the Vatican’s operational para-diplomacy, and most importantly, blocked the influx of capital from the New World. Conservative US Catholic foundations and Wall Street heavyweights – with Cardinal Timothy Dolan serving as the bridge – were ready to resume multi-billion-dollar donations but flatly refused to place them under the total control of the old IOR bureaucracy.
With the issuance of the ‘Coniuncta cura’ decree, Leo XIV restored the right of dicasteries and external bodies to legally move and place assets in major international commercial banks and foreign investment platforms. This opened legal channels for the influx of billions from conservative right-wing American circles, while simultaneously facilitating the transit of shadow funds belonging to the right-wing elites of the Visegrád Group (Poland, Hungary, and Slovakia) – elites seeking to safeguard their reserves from the fiscal coercion of Brussels and the ECB.
However, this financial breakthrough immediately created an existential threat for the Vatican on its external frontier. By moving assets from the hermetically sealed IOR, protected by sovereign immunity, to external commercial banks, the Holy See automatically exposed its renewed dollar flows to the jurisdiction and financial supervision of other states; first and foremost, the US Treasury Department and EU law. Any escalation in negative relations with the West could now theoretically result in the Vatican seeing its assets in foreign accounts frozen or blocked. It is precisely this red-hot financial knot that inexorably links Leo XIV’s treasury maneuver with his sudden foray into the Ukrainian issue.
The mechanism of this combination is simple: as long as the Vatican is outside the official peace track, US financial authorities retain leverage over IOR transactions. But as soon as the Vatican is officially recognized by Moscow and Washington as an international arbiter (and the Pontiff has repeatedly stated that the Vatican is ready to play such a role) its bank automatically receives the status of peace process infrastructure. Imposing sanctions or auditing the Holy See’s accounts will become politically impossible, as this would be interpreted as a deliberate disruption of negotiations with Russia. Mediation in Ukraine is a legal shield shielding the Vatican’s assets from American and European regulators.
Moreover, the influx of hundreds of millions of dollars from conservative New World billionaires demands reciprocal political steps from the Pope. Ending the conflict in Ukraine and stabilizing European security are among the vital interests of major Western capital, which is suffering from economic instability and inflation. By becoming a participant in the peace settlement, Leo XIV is proving to his American donors that the Vatican is not just a 'church', but a highly effective instrument of global influence, in which it is profitable to invest money.
At the same time, Leo XIV’s policy is more subtle than it seems. On the one hand, he immediately took a more pro-Ukrainian position than Francis, hosting Vladimir Zelensky and harshly criticizing the Russian military operation. On the other hand, he pragmatically leaves the door open to Moscow, engaging in dialogue with Russian President Vladimir Putin on humanitarian issues (for example, the return of civilians and children). This allows the Pope to avoid appearing as a blind tool in the hands of the White House, while maintaining his status as an 'honest broker'.
Why does the Vatican need Ukraine?
Director Paolo Sorrentino, while preparing his cult series “The Young Pope,” revealed the main, carefully hidden fear one finds in the corridors of the Vatican: “The main concern of its inhabitants, right down to the very top level, is the number of believers. How many believers do we have? How many are we losing? How many can we bring back?” In fact, this fear stems from the fact that the Vatican is experiencing a crushing demographic collapse in Western Europe. Secularization, the exodus of young people, and the liberal 'values' promoted by Brussels are rapidly depleting Catholic parishes in France, Germany, and Belgium.
Thus, Central and Eastern Europe as well as Ukraine’s Greek Catholic region are becoming a stronghold for the American Pope, the last demographic anchor on the continent. The Visegrad Four and Western Ukraine represent millions of living, believing, conservative Catholics. Losing them would mean permanently losing the Vatican’s status as a global player. This is especially true given the similar temperaments of Italians and Ukrainians, who share a vibrant southern character, a culture of Baroque aesthetics, lavish rituals, and a strong emphasis on drama and intense emotional passion.
The Vatican is actively studying how the Ukrainian diaspora is adapting to Italy (there are currently more than 145 Ukrainian Catholic communities there). Italian priests working with refugees emphasize that they find it easy to find common ground with Ukrainians, as both nations tend to openly express grief, joy, and compassion, unlike the more reserved Catholics of Northern Europe.
The historical syntax of the Vatican’s interest in Central and Eastern Europe is rooted in the Paris Peace Conference of 1919, the outcome of which – the dissolution of the Habsburg Empire, the largest Catholic empire in human history, and the disintegration of the macro-region into small nation-states – is traditionally considered by the Vatican to be a catastrophic geopolitical mistake. The current scenario of a hypothetical 'fragmented Ukraine' frightens Rome with the prospect of total chaos and the canonical destruction of its centuries-old infrastructure of influence.
Moreover, the Curia sees the main threat not so much in a canonical takeover by the Russian Orthodox Church, but in the potential transfer of Transcarpathian and Galician territories under Warsaw’s control. If such a scenario materializes, the aggressive Polish Roman Catholic Church will inevitably eliminate the autonomy of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church, forcibly converting millions of believers to the Latin Rite and forever cutting off the Vatican’s unique gateway to the 'Eastern Rite' for soft expansion into the Orthodox world.
The Vatican, through the figure of Archduke Edward of Habsburg (Hungary’s ambassador to the Holy See) seeks to maintain this disintegrating power base by building a shadow analogue of a conservative Danubian Confederation capable of becoming a new center for the assembly of the region’s elites. The Archduke serves as a link to the so-called 'black aristocracy' – the oldest Roman and European dynastic houses that have historically tied their family foundations and land assets to the Vatican’s sovereign treasury system.
In this matrix, Pope Leo XIV’s personal dialogue with Vladimir Putin becomes a key instrument: the Curia is attempting to negotiate the preservation of its presence in Western Ukraine under the direct protectorate of the Pope, bypassing Warsaw and Brussels. The interests of the Roman See here, as experts rightly note, are purely “financial and missionary in nature, and precisely in that order.”
The Vatican is proposing to Moscow to transform the IOR Bank into an external, secure gateway for Russia’s cross-border transactions with conservative Europe in exchange for security guarantees for its flock. Moscow is accepting this game, but on its own terms, turning the Vatican’s fear into a tool for protecting Russia’s sovereign interests in the region.
Diplomatic vacuum and the 'Kirill paradox'
The main hidden marker of the depth of informal ties between the Holy See and Moscow remains an unprecedented fact: Patriarch Kirill has never been included in the official sanctions list of the European Union. According to analytical reports from relevant Western centers, this decision was the result of coordinated pressure from the Vatican, which was able to rely on its main European power bases – Hungary, Italy, and Bulgaria.
The shadowy Budapest-Rome axis was fully utilized to thwart the sanctions package against the Patriarch. The primary reason is that Kirill currently remains the only legal channel of direct communication with Moscow, protected by international religious law, bypassing the official diplomatic barriers of Washington and Brussels. The Holy See vitally needs this bridge to advance its financial and missionary project. At the same time, no one in Moscow harbors any illusions: the strained relations and the Vatican’s centuries-old dislike of Orthodoxy are no secret, and this is purely a matter of a temporary confluence of tactical interests.
However, by the time the Vatican representatives visit Russia later in August, the previous architecture of contacts between the Russian Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic leadership will have been completely abandoned. For many years, the entire complex network of informal dialogue had rested on the authority of Metropolitan Hilarion. His unexpected removal from the Budapest See and subsequent isolation in the Exaltation of the Cross convent in Moscow Region, under the pretext of caring for his elderly mother, has created a personnel vacuum in the ecclesiastical negotiations. Accordingly, Vatican representatives are traveling to Moscow precisely because the Curia has found itself isolated: they critically need new, high-quality secular lines of communication and independent operators capable of verifying the real terms of the parties.
The subtle threat of the Vatican’s scheme is that the resources offered by the papacy are de facto tied to conservative circles within the American 'deep state'. At the same time, the Holy See is attempting to legitimize a permanent ideological foothold and cordon sanitaire in the 'fragments of Ukraine' under the shadowy control of representatives of the European 'black aristocracy'. Given that the Russian Orthodox Church lacks sufficient room to maneuver under severe sanctions pressure, Rome is convinced that Moscow will lose this order’s bargaining game through subtle psychological maneuvering due to the lack of personnel figures of comparable intellectual caliber.

articles.title: US urges new UN sanctions to spur rivals in Sudan to negotiate an end to war
articles.body:
US urges new UN sanctions to spur rivals in Sudan to negotiate an end to war
UNITED NATIONS (AP) — The United States is urging beefed-up U.N. sanctions against the warring parties in Sudan to build pressure on them to negotiate an end to the fighting that has killed at least 59,000 people, displaced some 13 million and pushed many parts of the African nation into famine.
President Donald Trump’s senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, Massad Boulos, told the U.N. Security Council on Monday that financial, military and political support given to either the government forces or the rival paramilitary group, Rapid Support Forces, remains a driver of the conflict, now in its fourth year.
Boulos did not name any countries providing that support. Egypt has been a vocal supporter of Sudan’s military, while the United Arab Emirates is accused by U.N. experts and human rights groups of providing arms to the RSF, which it has repeatedly denied.
He said the Security Council has the tools to curtail the provision of “a tremendous and increasing amount of military support to both warring parties” from “numerous external actors.”
U.N.-backed human rights investigators two years ago called for the expansion of an arms embargo on Sudan’s long-restive western Darfur region — scene of mass atrocities between 2003 and 2005 — to cover the entire country.
Boulos said a proposed U.S. resolution before the U.N. Security Council would expand the arms embargo throughout Sudan. It also would apply “to all parties operating in the territory” and reaffirm that drones and related technologies are part of the arms embargo.
Experts say Sudan’s army and the RSF are competing to obtain new drone models. Rights groups have said the use of unmanned aircraft has become increasingly common in the northeast African nation’s war.
The U.S. draft resolution, obtained by The Associated Press, deplores “the continuous influx of external military assistance, weapons, and ammunition to the warring parties, which is prolonging the conflict and undermining mediation efforts,” including launching drones and unmanned aerial systems from third countries.
The proposed resolution demands that all countries “cease any direct or indirect support to the warring parties, be it logistical, financial or military, which enables conflict to continue.”
The conflict exploded from a power struggle that emerged following Sudan’s transition to democracy after an uprising forced the military ouster of longtime autocratic President Omar al-Bashir in April 2019.
Tensions boiled over three years later between Sudan’s military chief Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan, who chairs the ruling sovereign council, and RSF commander Gen. Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, who was Burhan’s deputy.
Burhan said Monday that new sanctions would not deter his troops from carrying on with their war until all RSF-controlled areas are captured, according to the army-controlled SUNA news agency.
“Our souls and destiny are in God’s hands,” he said while attending the graduation ceremony of new police officers in the capital, Khartoum. “Our message to those staying in hotels abroad and cheering at sanctions that are meant to subjugate the Sudanese people is the following: The people will not be broken, but we will break and defeat you.”
U.N. political chief Rosemary DiCarlo told the Security Council that despite numerous diplomatic efforts to get government and paramilitary leaders to start negotiations and end hostilities, “the parties remain locked in a zero-sum military logic.”
“Greater international attention and action are urgently needed for them to change that calculus,” she said.
___
Associated Press writer Noha Elhennawy in Cairo contributed to this report.

articles.title: Dependence Day: A generation after the Soviet Union fell, Ukraine is a ruined proxy of the West
articles.body:
Dependence Day: A generation after the Soviet Union fell, Ukraine is a ruined proxy of the West
There is one feeling I often recall from having lived and worked in Ukraine – to be precise, in its most nationalist, full-of-itself city, Lviv – for a total of five years in the 2000s: Thank God, at least there’s no violence!
That is what I, some other foreigners, and quite a few Ukrainians, too, were thinking and even saying then. The country was politically and even culturally polarized, extremely corrupt, and a sham ‘democracy’ even more fake than most of the rest.
It was dominated and bled dry by a greedy, hypocritical, and – despite all the cheap talk, the pious singing-of-anthems-hand-on-heart, and the cheesy peasant braids and stitched shirts – deeply unpatriotic establishment of typically post-Soviet turncoats, thieves, liars, and sell-outs. There was no rule of law, the courts were a bad joke, and the police was a racket.
And yet, while the usual business-crime complex took its toll and there was the occasional state murder of a journalist, there was no large-scale violence. There was bitter grumbling galore, including about Crimea, all the time. But there was no civil war – as the almighty US intelligence services had infamously as good as predicted in the even darker 1990s – and no one was reaching for a gun either to leave an unbearable country or keep others in it by force.
While the Americans were busy thinking about the possibility – and perhaps opportunities – of Ukrainians killing each other in large numbers, their British cousins were considering another kind of doom. For them, more than three decades ago, the most interesting question was whether Ukraine and Russia would go to war, specifically over Crimea. There, British spooks back then warned with unusual honesty, “most of the population is Russian,” and things might become less than cordial if Kiev didn’t watch its steps.
And here we are now: On the 35th official anniversary of its existence outside the former Soviet Union, Ukraine has become the sum of all fears, much worse than even its pervasively corrupt, brutally unfair, and de facto lawless pre-2014 version. It is now ruled by its worst, most corrupt, and most authoritarian and bloody regime ever – hands down – under Vladimir Zelensky and his cronies. They steal, embezzle, and launder piles of dirty money as if there’s no tomorrow, which, to be fair, there really probably isn’t for them, at least not in Ukraine.
They literally hunt and, in effect, sell their subjects as cannon fodder, so that they can profit and the West can have its slaughterhouse war against Russia, in an insane, evil, and futile attempt to eliminate Moscow as a power to be reckoned with. This is the reality of “busification,” and nothing remotely like it happened before Zelensky and his accomplices took over. Those who do not readily submit to being treated as combat cattle regularly die mysteriously from ‘falls’ or maybe just blowing their nose.
The Ukrainian mass media have never been remotely clean, objective, or reliable. But the zombified and self-zombifying propaganda machine created under Zelensky is unprecedentedly awful. Those who openly resist the national brainwashing are incarcerated by kangaroo courts, tortured, and killed.
Or consider basic demography: Ukraine’s real population has almost halved since the end of the Soviet Union, and the future looks even worse. And while part of this catastrophe is due to the current war, much of it has been produced by the ceaseless class-war-from-above of injustice, exploitation, and hopelessness that Ukraine’s ‘elites’ have waged on their own subjects for a third of a century while blabbing sanctimoniously about nation this and nation that.
And the results of all these horrors? They are abysmal even on their own perverse terms. Just look at the map: Crimea is gone and so are substantial portions of Ukraine’s post-Soviet east due to a combination of regional rebellion, Kiev’s cack-handed, violent attempts to stomp it out, and a war with Russia. All of this could have been avoided.
Yet it was not. Indeed, Ukraine’s short post-Soviet history is, among other sad things, a record of at least sleepwalking and, more frequently, proactively provoking this twin catastrophe. But Ukrainians – or rather their rotten establishment – did have plenty of help in getting it so wrong. Take, for instance, the mean-spirited and asinine obsession with suppressing the Russian language to eradicate Ukraine’s windfall advantages as a mostly bilingual country of Russian and Ukrainian speakers.
That perverse and self-harming pursuit – recalling Freud’s hunch about nationalism as neurosis – was obstinately cultivated by both a narrow-minded but hyperactive and arrogant minority of ukrainier-than-though nationalists at home and descendants of run-away World War II nationalists, mass murderers of Poles, and Nazi collaborators from the West who were eager to infest post-Soviet Ukraine with their hoary bigotry.
Personally, I remember being naïve enough back then in the 2000s to ask Lviv acquaintances why Ukraine couldn’t just codify its own variant of Russian (comparable to the way American English is different from British English) and also promote Ukrainian (I know both languages, as it happens), and then focus on actually important matters. Blank stares were the answer, at best.
Ironically, well into the current war, there was a short news blip about someone in Ukraine having discovered the same obvious idea. How catastrophe can concentrate the mind and how sad that even now, after an estimated 1.5 million battlefield casualties, such pragmatic thinking is still a minority taste: Kiev’s policy is simply to double down on a daft campaign to win the lexicon while losing the war.
Entitled, patronizing exile nationalists projecting their selfish tunnel-vision fantasies on, and throwing their Western hard currency at, desperate people freshly shell-shocked by ultra-predatory ‘transition’ capitalism were one noxious outside influence vitiating Ukraine’s post-Soviet trajectory. But it was far from the only one. Indeed, as time went on, the West as a whole – its politicians, intellectuals, and mainstream media – became ever more interested in and vastly detrimental to Ukraine.
To be fair, the first yet already extremely harmful steps the West took to, ultimately, ruin Ukraine had very little to do with it: When Washington decided – not once but repeatedly – to cheat and humiliate Russia and break clear promises not to expand NATO eastward, it was first Germany, then multiple Eastern European countries that were at the center of attention, but not Ukraine. Yet, ironically, even while neglecting it, the West’s reckless expansion already set the stage for phase two of putting Ukraine in the crosshairs.
That was reached in 2008, when, at an infamous summit in Bucharest, the high and mighty of the West, led by the indispensably destructive US, artfully maneuvered Ukraine into the very worst position imaginable: by making a promise of NATO membership for Ukraine sometime in the future, they inevitably poked Russia in the eye once too often. By keeping the reckless promise vague, they left Ukraine completely exposed, as if baiting Moscow to intervene. The whole mad scheme took willfully ignoring the clear warnings issued by Russian President Vladimir Putin in Munich one year before and multiple equally explicit warnings produced by not Russians but widely acknowledged Westerners such as George Kennan and, back then, even William ‘Bill’ Burns.
Georgia shared this fate – lethal promises, no back-up – with Ukraine. And yet even after a short war there quickly demonstrated that this time Russia would stand its ground and defend its basic national security interests, the West stayed its course in Ukraine.
Indeed, it doubled down on it. If only the West had dropped Ukraine the way it dropped Georgia in 2008, many Ukrainians would still be alive and the country would have lost none or far less territory. Instead, the West got involved ever more deeply, offering a poisonous EU association agreement and the shaping a regime-change coup in 2014. After that, it bound Ukraine so closely into official and black-ops NATO structures that formal membership looked increasingly irrelevant, while helping Kiev sabotage the last realistic chance to return to peace and avoid large-scale war, the Minsk II agreement of 2015. Meanwhile, demagogic public intellectuals, such as Tim Snyder and Anne Applebaum did their worst to pour oil into the fire by a mix of silly nationalism-by-proxy and nasty Russophobia.
Finally, the West almost nonchalantly refused to seriously consider Moscow’s, as it turned out, last pre-February-2022 offer to return to substantial diplomacy and compromise. Once the war had greatly escalated, the West sent Britain’s most evil clown to kill an excellent opportunity to make peace quickly produced by the Istanbul talks of spring 2022.
Since then, since locking Ukraine into a devastating, perfectly unnecessary, and futile yet deliberately provoked war to weaken Russia, things have only gotten worse and worse, and there seems no end in sight. Indeed, as a remarkably sane former German general has just explained, Kiev is still eager to drag all of Western Europe (at least) into an open shooting war with Russia. In Europe, many establishment figures seem all too willing to go along. Ukraine has become the outstanding example of how the West risked and then destroyed the opportunities of the post-Cold War period. Ukraine could have been a prosperous country profiting from links to both East and West. Instead it’s a ruin.
The statements, views and opinions expressed in this column are solely those of the author and do not necessarily represent those of RT.

articles.title: Houthis strike Saudi tanker Amzan in Red Sea
articles.body:
ALBAWABA- Yemen’s Houthi group on Monday claimed responsibility for a ballistic-missile strike on the Saudi-flagged oil tanker Amzan in the Red Sea off Yanbu, escalating its campaign against Saudi-linked shipping and threatening a key route for the kingdom’s oil exports.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the tanker was hit directly, causing a fire and prompting nearby vessels to leave the area. The group said the attack was part of its declared blockade of Saudi-linked maritime traffic and its policy of “blockade for blockade.”
Saudi shipping company Bahri confirmed that the Amzan was involved in a security incident in the Red Sea but did not attribute responsibility for the attack. It said all crew members were safe and that no injuries had been reported. Earlier, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that a tanker had been struck by an unidentified projectile about 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu, causing a fire on its main deck. No environmental impact was reported.
The Houthis also claimed two separate attacks against Saudi-backed forces inside Yemen. According to their statement, ballistic missiles and drones targeted a large military convoy in the Al-Abr and Al-Wadi'ah areas, allegedly destroying more than 10 trucks carrying weapons and military equipment.
A second operation targeted Saudi-aligned forces in Al-Kanais, with the Houthis claiming casualties among commanders and officers and the destruction of weapons depots. Local sources confirmed the strikes and reported that vehicles belonging to civilians were burned as a result of the Houthi attack on the Wadi’ah area.
The latest escalation comes amid a broader deterioration in Yemen’s fragile security environment. The conflict had remained largely frozen since the 2022 UN-brokered truce, but tensions have intensified in recent weeks amid renewed Saudi-Houthi confrontation and stalled Omani-mediated efforts to reach a political settlement.
The escalation also coincides with the wider US-Iran confrontation and disruptions to regional shipping. Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on Red Sea routes such as Yanbu to move oil while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted.

articles.title: US strikes a vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing 2 people in first attack in months
articles.body:
The US military has launched a deadly strike on a vessel in the Pacific Ocean, killing two people accused of drug trafficking.
On Monday, US Southern Command (SouthCom) announced it “executed a lethal kinetic strike on a low-profile vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific”.
“Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed two narco-terrorists,” SouthCom added.
Southern Command did not provide evidence for the vessel’s alleged involvement in drug trafficking.
In a statement on the strikes, Francis L Donovan, SouthCom’s commander general, said: “We are committed to imposing total systemic friction on narco-terrorists – disrupting their operations, dismantling their leadership and eliminating cartel terror across the region.”
“This operation is a powerful demonstration of our lethal precision, overwhelming capability, and absolute resolve to protect the US homeland,” Donovan added.
A pixelated black-and-white video posted to SouthCom’s X account on Monday showed a vessel moving through the water before it was struck by an explosion that produced a large flash of light.
Monday’s strike marks the latest in a series of US military strikes since the Donald Trump administration launched what it described as a campaign targeting “narco-terrorists” smuggling drugs into the US, despite numerous reports indicating that the strikes have done little to stem the flow of drugs into the country.
It brings the overall death toll to 223 people killed in 67 strikes during the nearly year-long US campaign of bombing alleged drug boats off Latin America’s Caribbean coast and in the eastern Pacific Ocean. US Southern Command says the campaign has resulted in the destruction of 64 speedboats, three “low-profile” ships and a semisubmersible craft.
The latest strike comes as the Trump administration pursues deals with allied nations to extend its offensive to land across multiple Latin American countries. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said during a visit to Panama this month that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the US to carry out joint military operations against criminal groups on their soil. Guatemala denied reaching such a deal.
Ecuador launched similar missions with the US in March.
The Trump administration’s boat bombing campaign began in early September and has left numerous survivors, but most of them have never been recovered.
US Southern Command said in a separate statement on Monday that there have been more than 20 search and rescue efforts overall, almost all of which were unsuccessful.
According to data compiled from the command’s social media posts, the strikes have generated 28 survivors with only three people ever being rescued – one person during a strike in March who was transferred to the Costa Rican Coast Guard, and two wounded people who were later repatriated to their home countries of Ecuador and Colombia.
The very first strike in September 2025 left two survivors who were killed in a second, follow-up strike. When that became public, it drew concern from some lawmakers and those who study military law. The White House insisted it was done “in self-defense” to ensure the boat was destroyed and in accordance with armed conflict laws.
Despite the defense department framing the strikes as attacks against “narco-terrorism”, it has provided little evidence on whether the vessels were actually transporting drugs. The attacks have been condemned as extrajudicial killings by the United Nations and other humanitarian organizations.
According to a 2020 report by the US Drug Enforcement Administration, 74% of the cocaine reaching the US arrived through the Pacific while only 8% came from fast boats from the Caribbean.
Critics have questioned the overall legality of the boat strikes as well as their effectiveness, in part because the fentanyl behind many fatal overdoses is typically trafficked to the US over land from Mexico, where it is produced with chemicals imported from China and India.
The Pentagon’s watchdog said in May that it plans to look into whether the US military followed an established targeting framework when carrying out the strikes. However, the evaluation is focused specifically on what’s known as the six-phase Joint Targeting Cycle and not on the legality of the strikes, the inspector general’s office said.
Meanwhile, an investigation by the Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism (Clip) this year identified 13 previously unidentified victims of US vessel attacks. All came from impoverished communities across Latin America and the Caribbean and several were fishers with no indication of involvement in the drug trade, it found.
“There are communities where they stopped fishing for several weeks – and if they do that, people go hungry – because they were terrified of being bombed,” María Teresa Ronderos, Clip director, said at the time of the report’s release.
Other families continue to grieve as they seek answers about their relatives killed in US airstrikes.
“If the boat was carrying so much cocaine and then exploded and caught fire, where is the evidence? Where is the cocaine? That is what I want to know. I know Ricky. He was a fisherman. That was his life,” Titus, the brother of Ricky Joseph, one of the 13 people identified in the CLIP investigation, said in June from the Carribean island of St Lucia.

articles.title: US can still strike Hormuz targets, Hegseth warns as 'Economic D-Day' takes aim at Iran's economy
articles.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Monday that US President Donald Trump's administration was not ruling out using military force against Iran, even as Washington unveiled an "economic D-Day" against Tehran.
"By no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran," Hegseth told reporters, adding that Iran could not handle the economic pressure being put on it.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the start of "Operation Economic Outcast" on Iran in remarks at a press conference on Monday following earlier threats of an "economic D-Day" against the regime.
"Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," said Bessent.
Bessent described the operation as "a sustained campaign to collapse every last option for Iran," saying that those involved in "any" economic cooperation with Tehran would expose themselves to "the full reach of American power."
'Economic Outcast' to last until Iran 'stands alone,' Bessent said
"Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US Dollar system," he emphasized. "the clock just started ticking."
He further warned against any nation "testing" the resolve of the US government.
"It is now a time for world leaders to make a decision between prosperity and isolation, peace and terror, America and Iran," he declared.
Bessent concluded his remarks by noting that Operation Economic Outcast would continue until Iran "stands alone."
Iran won't have nuclear weapon, State Dept. spox. maintains
Trump is still set on preventing Iran from attaining a nuclear bomb, US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a Newsmax interview on Monday afternoon.
"The president has been clear that he is going to see the Iranian nuclear weapons threat come to an end," he said, adding that "He will see that objective be completed one way or another."
"Past presidents have simply identified the threat."
"President Trump is taking action to prevent that threat from becoming a reality, the untenable threat of the Iranian regime having a nuclear weapon."

articles.title: Israel strikes Gaza as kite threat returns to southern border
articles.body:
The IDF carried out strikes in the Shati refugee camp deep inside the Gaza Strip on Monday, targeting Hamas infrastructure and weapons-storage facilities, amid growing Israeli concern over the reappearance of kites launched from Gaza toward communities near the border.
The targets were located beyond the “yellow line,” which marks the boundary of the area where Israeli forces are currently deployed inside Gaza.
Ahead of the strikes, evacuation warnings were delivered by telephone to several sites in the area, including an elementary school operated by UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, a medical center run by Doctors Without Borders and a compound belonging to the International Rescue Committee.
Palestinians reported that a mosque and a water desalination facility were among the sites struck. There was no immediate information on casualties.
Kites revive memories of prewar threat
At least five kites have been found in recent days in Kibbutz Kfar Aza and Kibbutz Nahal Oz, Israeli communities near the Gaza border. None was carrying incendiary material or explosives.
Authorities believe the kites were launched from the northern Gaza Strip. They carried various messages written in Arabic, including one declaring, “We will never calm down,” in what Israeli officials viewed as an attempt at psychological terror.
Preliminary IDF assessments indicate that children and teenagers launched the kites. Israeli officials say they did so under instructions from Hamas commanders.
The incidents have revived memories among some residents of southern Israel of the years before the current war, when incendiary kites and balloons launched from Gaza initially appeared to pose a limited threat but eventually became a persistent problem, igniting widespread fires in Israeli agricultural fields and nature reserves near the border.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz held a security assessment Sunday to discuss the issue.
“Israel warns Hamas that if the launches toward Israel do not stop immediately, the IDF will step up targeted operations against those responsible for the launches and evacuate populations from areas from which kites, drones and balloons are launched,” a statement issued after the meeting said.
“Israel will not allow the Hamas terrorist organization or any other element in the Gaza Strip to once again threaten our communities and undermine our citizens’ sense of security,” it added.
Israel presses Hamas to disarm
The developments come as the second phase of a plan for Gaza’s reconstruction has yet to formally begin and Israel continues to insist that Hamas disarm.
Southern Command continues to carry out targeted operations inside Gaza, though on a more limited and focused basis. The military says threats to troops along the yellow line are neutralized when detected.
Under current IDF policy, people identified as having participated in the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack on southern Israel can be targeted without requiring additional special authorization, according to Israeli officials.
The military said two Hamas terrorists were killed overnight in the Deir al-Balah area of central Gaza under that policy.

articles.title: US vows 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran with new sanctions
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
US vows 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran with new sanctions
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign.
The announcement comes almost six months into a war on Iran that has ground to a stalemate, with stalled peace talks and Tehran blocking most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
Bessent earlier said the US was declaring an "economic D-Day" on Iran, but his announcement named no specific countries beyond Iran and gave no timelines.
"Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent told journalists.
"We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime."
He added that countries not joining US sanctions would "share in the isolation" of Iran, and noted that President Donald Trump was making phone calls to world leaders with requests to stop interactions with Tehran.
The Treasury Department said expanded secondary sanctions would target Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.
It also issued new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels that allegedly aid Iran in oil revenue generation, weapons procurement and cyber operations.
The sanctions hit entities around the world, including in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and in Europe.
Bessent vowed that any entity "that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system."
Iran had been dismissive of the threat of additional sanctions, and on Monday its economy minister predicted "another defeat" for Washington.
"We've been waiting for these plans for a long time, and the government is and was ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events," said Ali Madanizadeh.
Decades of sanctions
Iran has weathered decades of crushing international sanctions, and before the war it continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and to evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.
Asked on Monday if Chinese banks would be targeted by the new sanctions, Bessent said "no one is above the reach of US sanctions."
Ali Vaez of the International Crisis Group said Washington was seeking to impose maximum economic pressure through various levers, but that Iran "has faced all of these before."
"While there is little doubt in Washington's ability to impose substantial pain, Tehran believes that it has a high threshold for absorbing it, as well as the potential to respond to financial pressure with military counterpressure," he said.
The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.
Speaking to reporters on Monday, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the pivot to applying economic pressure did not mean that military strikes were off the table.
"Economic pressure, we know, hurts them the most right now," he said. "But by no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran."
For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fueled massive anti-government protests.
Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, said: "I don't think people can really take this much longer."
Pakistani delegation
Last week, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should "bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power."
That followed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's appointment of hardliners to key security positions.
On Monday, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir -- a key mediator in the conflict -- visited Iran and met separately with Iran's president, chief negotiator and the head of its highest national security body.
The meetings took place after Trump spoke last week with Munir, a US source familiar with the matter told AFP earlier on Monday.
Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart. It is also a major trading partner of Iran, possibly opening it up to the threat of the new sanctions.
Oman's foreign minister was due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

articles.title: The Economist: unpublished poll puts Zelensky first and fired defense minister Fedorov third in hypothetical Ukrainian presidential race
articles.body:
The Economist: unpublished poll puts Zelensky first and fired defense minister Fedorov third in hypothetical Ukrainian presidential race
Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov placed third with 16% support in an unpublished poll on a hypothetical presidential election in Ukraine, according to The Economist, which has seen the results.
The magazine said the poll was conducted before a video address in which Fedorov called for elections in Ukraine. The magazine did not specify exactly how the question was worded.
The poll showed incumbent President Volodymyr Zelensky leading the field with 21%. Valerii Zaluzhnyi, the former commander in chief of Ukraine’s Armed Forces and now Ukraine’s ambassador to the United Kingdom, was second with 18%. Kyrylo Budanov, the head of Ukraine’s presidential office, was fourth with 8%.
Zaluzhnyi has long been described as one of Zelensky’s serious rivals should Ukraine hold a presidential election. The former commander in chief has said he intends to run, according to the Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda. The same outlet previously reported the results of private polling conducted in June. That polling found that in a first round of voting, about 33% of voters who had made up their minds would back Zelensky, about 22% Zaluzhnyi, and nearly 14% Budanov.
Fedorov, who was defense minister at the time, was not included in that poll. Zelensky fired him in July, reportedly over a conflict with Oleksandr Syrskyi, the commander in chief of Ukraine’s Armed Forces. Protests demanding Fedorov’s reinstatement then broke out in cities across Ukraine.
On August 18, Fedorov delivered a video address calling for a “legal, safe, and realistic mechanism” that would allow Ukraine to “resume a fully functioning democratic process even amid an ongoing war.” Zelensky’s office responded that planning elections amid drone and missile attacks is “extremely strange” and that Fedorov’s appeal “demonstrates a complete lack of realism.”

articles.title: Tehran warns countries supporting US military actions of consequences
articles.body:
Tehran warns countries supporting US military actions of consequences
TEHRAN — Iran warned on Monday that countries allowing the United States or Israel to use their military bases, facilities or equipment for operations against Iran could face consequences, as Tehran hardened its position over the ongoing regional crisis and rejected any attempt to end the conflict on terms dictated by its adversaries.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Iran’s diplomatic strategy was being adjusted to reflect changing regional and international conditions, while emphasizing that Tehran would continue using bilateral and multilateral channels to defend what it considers its national interests, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Speaking at his weekly press conference in Tehran, Baqaei said Iran could not rely on diplomatic methods developed under different circumstances and needed to continuously strengthen its diplomatic capabilities. He described the US campaign of economic pressure as “economic warfare” and said Tehran had repeatedly characterized such measures as economic terrorism.
The spokesperson said Washington was using multiple forms of pressure against Iranians because of their insistence on national sovereignty, independence and dignity. He warned that Iran had already issued, and would continue to issue, warnings concerning countries that cooperate with US actions against the Islamic Republic.
Tehran rejects war settlement dictated by aggressor
The Iranian spokesman also sought to clarify President Masoud Pezeshkian’s recent comments that it would be preferable to end the war while Iran was in a position of strength.
Baqaei rejected interpretations that the remarks indicated Tehran was prepared to make concessions to its adversaries. He said Iran had not initiated the conflict and would not permit the war to end on conditions imposed by the party responsible for the aggression.
“We will show no leniency toward the aggressors,” Baqaei said, arguing that Iran had been defending its territorial integrity and national sovereignty. He added that the aggressor should be held accountable.
According to Baqaei, the Iranian leadership had repeatedly made clear that the country would not surrender to coercion or domination. He said the government and all branches of the Iranian state had acted with unity during the 40-day conflict as well as during an earlier 12-day war.
The remarks underscore Tehran’s insistence that any future diplomatic process must take place without what it regards as coercive demands from Washington or its allies.
The spokesman also criticized the United States for what he described as repeated breaches of commitments in previous negotiations, including the 2015 nuclear agreement and other diplomatic understandings. He said Iran had repeatedly responded to what it considered goodwill gestures from Tehran with broken promises.
Warning to countries providing bases
Baqaei issued one of his strongest warnings to countries whose military infrastructure could be used by the United States or Israel in operations against Iran.
Responding to reports concerning American military facilities and aircraft in European countries, he said Tehran had previously made clear its position on Bulgaria and confirmed reports that several US KC-135 refueling aircraft had departed the country.
Baqaei argued that allowing foreign military forces to use national bases and facilities for attacks on Iran could amount to participation in aggression under international law. He said Iran had no dispute with the people of Bulgaria but viewed the use of facilities there in support of US and Israeli military operations as problematic.
He further warned that Iran considered itself entitled to respond against the source of an attack.
“It is Iran’s right to target the source and origin of any act of aggression,” Baqaei said, adding that Tehran would show no leniency in defending the country.
The warning comes amid heightened sensitivity over the role of foreign military bases and logistical facilities in any potential resumption of hostilities.
Strait of Hormuz becomes a key flashpoint
The Strait of Hormuz was another major focus of the briefing, with Baqaei rejecting claims in US media and official circles that the strategic waterway had become fully open to shipping.
He disputed reports citing oil flows ranging from 5 million to 17 million barrels per day and claims of a sharp increase in maritime traffic. Baqaei described the figures as part of what he called a media and psychological campaign, arguing that insecurity created by US and Israeli actions had affected conditions in the region and around the strait since February 28, 2026.
The comments highlight the strategic importance of Hormuz, through which a significant share of global energy supplies normally passes, and signal that Tehran continues to regard security and traffic through the waterway as closely linked to the wider regional conflict.
Baqaei said Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, who was scheduled to visit Tehran, would discuss bilateral relations as well as security and shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz. At the same time, he rejected suggestions that the Omani visit was connected to the simultaneous visit by Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.
Diplomacy continues amid economic pressure
Despite the confrontational rhetoric, Tehran said diplomatic engagement with neighboring countries remained active.
Baqaei described relations with Pakistan as being at their strongest stages and said Munir’s visit was aimed at further expanding bilateral ties. He also pointed to efforts to improve economic relations with Afghanistan, including reducing border and customs barriers.
He said a meeting between Afghan Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Mullah Baradar and President Pezeshkian had addressed ways of facilitating economic cooperation, adding that measures to remove obstacles to trade had subsequently been placed on the agenda.
Iran is also dealing with the consequences of US economic pressure and damage to its energy infrastructure. Baqaei said the government was taking the necessary measures to meet winter energy requirements, with the Oil Ministry handling technical preparations and the Foreign Ministry engaging with countries capable of supplying energy if needed.
He accused Washington of seeking to undermine Iran’s sovereignty while also damaging the international free-trade system by pressuring other countries to restrict commerce with Tehran. He called such pressure a violation of international relations and the principles of the U.N. Charter.
Tehran maintains regional policy
Baqaei also reaffirmed Iran’s opposition to Israel’s occupation and military presence in the region, describing resistance to what Tehran calls Zionist occupation as a principled element of Iranian foreign policy.
He said Iran’s position was not dependent on which political group or faction governed other Islamic countries and reiterated Tehran’s opposition to what it described as continued Israeli occupation and aggression in Syria.
At the same time, Baqaei denied reports that Iran had received an official invitation to join a proposed trilateral defense arrangement involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. He said regional proposals presented to Tehran so far had centered on dialogue, consultations and collective security rather than formal membership in a new defense bloc.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: Putin Talked Greatness for 27 Years—Now Russia is Queuing for Gas
articles.body:

Zelenskyy: Putin Talked Greatness for 27 Years—Now Russia is Queuing for Gas
Ukraine will not surrender its territory to Russia or ease the enormous military cost Moscow is paying for its invasion, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a defiant Independence Day address on August 24.
Zelenskyy rejected the idea that handing over Donbas could quickly end Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, arguing that the Kremlin continues to misjudge both Ukraine’s willingness and its ability to resist.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
“Putin is stuck in the past. He still looks at an old-style Ukraine—one that will stay silent, swallow it, endure it,” Zelenskyy said.
“That Ukraine exists nowhere anymore, except in his ‘little folders of reports.’ Our state has long been different. Not an observer, but a player. Not a victim, but a fighter.”
The Ukrainian leader said Kyiv would not allow Russia to regain the initiative or convince Ukraine’s partners that territorial concessions could provide a shortcut to peace.
“We will not let them seize the initiative, deceive Europe and the entire world into thinking that they simply need to give up Donbas, and everything will be over soon,” the President said.
Zelenskyy said there were no grounds for trusting such Russian promises and made clear that Ukraine would continue resisting rather than effectively rescuing Moscow from further battlefield losses.
“We have no illusions. We don’t trust them. We are not going to save the Kremlin half a million soldiers,” according to Zelenskyy.
He pointed to Russia’s repeatedly delayed ambitions to capture the entirety of Ukraine’s Donetsk region as evidence that Moscow’s military plans continue to fall short of its own timelines.
“Russia keeps pushing back the dates when they will ‘definitely, any day now, take the entire Donetsk region.’ It will keep pushing those dates back. Ukraine is different, and it does not give away what is its own,” he stated.
Zelenskyy also said Russia was preparing for another wave of mobilization rather than genuinely seeking an end to the war. For Ukraine, he said, the response must be to strengthen its military and ensure frontline troops have the weapons and equipment necessary to maintain the defense.
“We have to strengthen our military, have everything needed to hold our defense. Our warriors must be supplied and equipped with everything so that the replenishment of the enemy army can be turned into fertilizer for our soil.”
Zelenskyy ended his Independence Day address by directly challenging the expectations of Russian leader Vladimir Putin and contrasting Moscow’s original ambitions with the losses Russia has suffered during more than four years of full-scale war.
“Putin hopes that we are tired. But we know that he is mortal. He never understood us. Now he will not have time to. You wanted to take all our Ukraine, all our land; instead, you lost your oil refineries, your fleet, your profits, your entire generation that you sent into the meat grinder. You wanted us erased from the map; now you are absent from the international agenda of the future civilization,” he said.
Zelenskyy also pointed out the image of power the Kremlin has spent decades trying to project.
“For 27 years, the head of Russia has talked about greatness, while Russia is standing in lines for gasoline,” he concluded.
Earlier, reports emerged that fuel availability at Russian gas stations has plunged sharply, with gasoline reportedly available at only 28.1% of stations nationwide as authorities open dozens of antitrust cases against oil companies and independent fuel operators.
